beats.text: On January first, twenty twenty-seven, Ottawa lets you earn more before federal tax. Manitoba doesn't.
The federal basic personal amount rises from sixteen thousand four hundred fifty-two dollars to sixteen thousand eight hundred seventy-nine. The brackets move up too.
That's four hundred twenty-seven dollars more tax-free. At fourteen percent, about sixty dollars less federal tax.
Plus a proposed cut: the base CPP rate drops from four point nine five to four point seven five percent. Up to one hundred forty-six dollars a year back on your pay.
The catch in Manitoba: no indexing for twenty twenty-seven. The provincial basic amount stays at fifteen thousand seven hundred eighty.
Check your first pay stub in January, and update your TD1 if your situation changed.
Next: part-time or full-time, what you really keep. Follow so you don't miss it.
